knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Kengo 2024 asked whether adding clofazimine to a drug-resistant tuberculosis
regimen changes the pharmacokinetics of four co-administered drugs. Clofazimine
was withheld for the first two weeks of treatment, and pharmacokinetic sampling
was done on day 14 (visit 1, no clofazimine) and again 21 days after clofazimine
was started (visit 2). The paper developed three new population PK models,
each packaged here as its own model file:

* `Kengo_2024_isoniazid` -- two-compartment model with well-stirred hepatic
  first-pass extraction and NAT2-phenotype-dependent intrinsic clearance; no
  clofazimine effect.
* `Kengo_2024_linezolid` -- one-compartment model with transit absorption; no
  clofazimine effect.
* `Kengo_2024_levofloxacin` -- one-compartment model with transit absorption,
  a creatinine-clearance effect on clearance and a 14.8% lower clearance with
  clofazimine.

The other two drugs were described with previously published models and are
not packaged from this paper. Clofazimine concentrations were predicted by the
three-compartment model of Abdelwahab et al. 2020
([doi:10.1093/jac/dkaa310](https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkaa310)) without
re-estimating any parameter. Cycloserine (dosed as terizidone, six
participants) used the model of Chirehwa et al. 2020
([doi:10.1128/AAC.01381-20](https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01381-20)); the paper
re-estimated its total clearance, but the change was not significant
(dOFV -2.16) and the re-estimated value is not reported, so the cycloserine
model is Chirehwa's unchanged.

```{r citations}
mod_inh <- readModelDb("Kengo_2024_isoniazid")
mod_lzd <- readModelDb("Kengo_2024_linezolid")
mod_lfx <- readModelDb("Kengo_2024_levofloxacin")
ui_inh <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_inh)
ui_lzd <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_lzd)
ui_lfx <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_lfx)
```

* Citation: `r ui_lfx$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01583-23>
* Description (isoniazid): `r ui_inh$description`
* Description (linezolid): `r ui_lzd$description`
* Description (levofloxacin): `r ui_lfx$description`

# Population

The cohort was 27 newly diagnosed adults with pulmonary drug-resistant
tuberculosis at Klerksdorp/Tshepong Hospital, North-West Province, South Africa
(Kengo 2024 Table 1). 19 (70%) were men and 23 (85%) were living with HIV;
median age was 39 years and median weight 52 kg. All 27 contributed isoniazid
data (high-dose isoniazid 450 or 600 mg daily, median 10.0 mg/kg; 5 slow, 13
intermediate and 9 rapid NAT2 acetylators), and 21 contributed linezolid (600 mg
daily) and levofloxacin (750 or 1000 mg daily) data. In the linezolid /
levofloxacin subset, median fat-free mass was 41.5 kg (range 26.0-51.6) and
median Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 81.8 mL/min (range 50.5-136).
Treatment was given under direct observation with a meal. Samples were drawn
pre-dose and 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 h after the observed dose at each visit.

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata, for example `readModelDb("Kengo_2024_levofloxacin")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to Kengo 2024 Table 2.
The tables below collect them. All typical values refer to a participant with
fat-free mass (FFM) 42 kg (Table 2 footnote a). Table 2 footnote g defines the
reported variability as %CV = sqrt(omega^2) * 100, so each variance is
(%CV / 100)^2.

|---|---|---|

| `lvc` | `log(57.0)` L | Table 2 central volume |

```{r variance-check}
# Each estimated variance reproduces its Table 2 %CV as sqrt(omega^2) * 100.
omega_tab <- function(ui) {
  d <- ui$iniDf
  d <- d[!is.na(d$neta1) & d$neta1 == d$neta2 & !d$fix, ]
  setNames(sqrt(d$est) * 100, d$name)
}
printed <- list(
  inh = c(etalclint = 16.2, etabvv_clint_1 = 18.4, etaiov_ka_1 = 94.3, etaiov_mtt_1 = 129, etaiov_fdepot_1 = 47.5),
  lzd = c(etalcl = 31.6, etabvv_cl_1 = 33.3, etaiov_ka_2 = 104, etaiov_mtt_2 = 73.8, etaiov_fdepot_2 = 12.4),
  lfx = c(etalcl = 18.3, etabvv_cl_1 = 17.0, etaiov_ka_2 = 118, etaiov_mtt_2 = 44.4, etaiov_fdepot_2 = 21.5)
)
got <- list(inh = omega_tab(ui_inh), lzd = omega_tab(ui_lzd), lfx = omega_tab(ui_lfx))
for (d in names(printed)) {
  stopifnot(setequal(names(got[[d]]), names(printed[[d]])))
  stopifnot(all(abs(got[[d]][names(printed[[d]])] - printed[[d]]) < 1e-6))
}

# The inflated (unobserved-dose) slots are the estimated variance times the
# squared Table 2 scaling factor.
infl <- function(ui, factor) {
  d <- ui$iniDf
  v <- setNames(d$est, d$name)
  c(
    ka = v[["etaiov_ka_1"]] / v[["etaiov_ka_2"]],
    mtt = v[["etaiov_mtt_1"]] / v[["etaiov_mtt_2"]],
    f = v[["etaiov_fdepot_1"]] / v[["etaiov_fdepot_2"]]
  ) / factor^2
}
# Tolerance 1e-4: the inflated variances are stored to 6-7 significant figures.
stopifnot(all(abs(infl(ui_lzd, 1.60) - 1) < 1e-4), all(abs(infl(ui_lfx, 1.99) - 1) < 1e-4))
```

# Structural checks

These checks use typical values only (`omega = NA`), so they are deterministic
and are asserted tightly.

```{r single-dose-mass-balance}
# One dose on an observed occasion (OCC = 2) for a typical 42 kg-FFM
# participant, followed long enough for the terminal phase to vanish.
sd_events <- function(dose, tend, extra = list()) {
  tt <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), seq(24, tend, by = 0.5))))
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = c(0, tt), amt = c(dose, rep(0, length(tt))),
    evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(tt))), cmt = "depot",
    FFM = 42, OCC = 2L
  )
  for (nm in names(extra)) ev[[nm]] <- extra[[nm]]
  ev
}
trap_auc <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

solve_det <- function(mod, ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
                  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6)
}

sd_lzd <- solve_det(mod_lzd, sd_events(600, 400))
sd_lfx <- solve_det(mod_lfx, sd_events(1000, 600, list(CRCL = 81.8, CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE = 0)))
nat2 <- data.frame(phenotype = c("slow", "intermediate", "rapid"),
                   NAT2_SLOW = c(1, 0, 0), NAT2_RAPID = c(0, 0, 1),
                   clint = c(12.2, 24.9, 46.7))
sd_inh <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(nat2)), function(i) {
  solve_det(mod_inh, sd_events(600, 1200, list(NAT2_SLOW = nat2$NAT2_SLOW[i], NAT2_RAPID = nat2$NAT2_RAPID[i])))
})

# AUC(0-inf) * CL equals the bioavailable dose. For isoniazid the systemic
# clearance is qh * eh and the bioavailable dose is fh * dose; their ratio
# collapses to the oral-clearance identity AUC = dose / (fu * CLint).
mb <- data.frame(
  model = c("linezolid", "levofloxacin", paste("isoniazid,", nat2$phenotype)),
  auc = c(trap_auc(sd_lzd$time, sd_lzd$Cc), trap_auc(sd_lfx$time, sd_lfx$Cc),
          vapply(sd_inh, function(s) trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc), numeric(1))),
  expected = c(600 / 3.04, 1000 / 6.81, 600 / (0.95 * nat2$clint))
)
mb$pct_diff <- 100 * (mb$auc / mb$expected - 1)
knitr::kable(mb, digits = 3, caption = "Single-dose AUC(0-inf) against the closed-form value.")
stopifnot(all(abs(mb$pct_diff) < 0.1))
```

The isoniazid identity confirms that the liver extracts the oral dose once on
its way in (fraction `fh` survives) and clears systemic drug at `qh * eh`. The
apparent oral clearances implied for a 42 kg-FFM participant are
`r paste(sprintf("%.1f", 0.95 * nat2$clint), collapse = ", ")` L/h for slow,
intermediate and rapid acetylators, against a hepatic plasma flow of 72.4 L/h
(first-pass extraction `r paste(sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * 0.95 * nat2$clint / (0.95 * nat2$clint + 72.4)), collapse = ", ")`).

```{r covariate-ratios}
# Levofloxacin covariate effects recovered from steady-state exposure. At
# steady state AUC(0-24) = F * dose / CL, so an AUC ratio is the inverse
# clearance ratio.
ss_events <- function(dose, extra) {
  doses <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 24 * 13, by = 24), amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 24 * 13 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "depot")
  ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
  ev$FFM <- 42
  ev$OCC <- 2L
  for (nm in names(extra)) ev[[nm]] <- extra[[nm]]
  ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}
auc_last_day <- function(extra) {
  s <- solve_det(mod_lfx, ss_events(1000, extra))
  trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc)
}
auc_ref <- auc_last_day(list(CRCL = 81.8, CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE = 0))
auc_cfz <- auc_last_day(list(CRCL = 81.8, CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE = 1))
auc_crcl <- auc_last_day(list(CRCL = 91.8, CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE = 0))
ratios <- data.frame(
  contrast = c("clofazimine vs none", "CLCR 91.8 vs 81.8 mL/min"),
  auc_ratio = c(auc_cfz / auc_ref, auc_crcl / auc_ref),
  expected = c(1 / (1 - 0.148), 1 / 1.047)
)
ratios$pct_diff <- 100 * (ratios$auc_ratio / ratios$expected - 1)
knitr::kable(ratios, digits = 4, caption = "Levofloxacin steady-state AUC ratios against the Table 2 effects.")
stopifnot(all(abs(ratios$pct_diff) < 0.1))
```

A 14.8% lower clearance raises the steady-state AUC by
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (ratios$auc_ratio[1] - 1))`, the "19% increase" in
levofloxacin AUC the paper reports (median 140 to 166 mg*h/L, a ratio of
`r sprintf("%.3f", 166 / 140)`).

# Virtual cohort

Covariates are drawn to match Table 1: sex (70% male in the isoniazid cohort,
62% in the linezolid / levofloxacin cohort), height, and weight log-normal
around the cohort median and truncated to the observed range. Fat-free mass
follows from sex, weight and height by the Janmahasatian equation. Creatinine
clearance is log-normal around the 81.8 mL/min median, truncated to 50.5-136
mL/min. Doses follow the weight-band assumptions in the Assumptions section.

```{r cohort}
ffm_janmahasatian <- function(wt, ht, female) {
  ifelse(female == 1,
         37.99 * ht^2 * wt / (35.98 * ht^2 + wt),
         42.92 * ht^2 * wt / (30.93 * ht^2 + wt))
}
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, median, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  x <- rlnorm(n, log(median), sdlog)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- rlnorm(sum(bad), log(median), sdlog)
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}
make_cohort <- function(n, male_frac, wt_median, wt_lo, wt_hi) {
  female <- rbinom(n, 1, 1 - male_frac)
  ht <- ifelse(female == 1, rnorm(n, 1.60, 0.06), rnorm(n, 1.70, 0.06))
  wt <- rtrunc_lnorm(n, wt_median, 0.15, wt_lo, wt_hi)
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), female = female, HT = ht, WT = wt,
             FFM = ffm_janmahasatian(wt, ht, female))
}

set.seed(20240410)
n_per_arm <- 150
cohort_inh <- make_cohort(3 * n_per_arm, 0.70, 53, 37, 66)
cohort_inh$phenotype <- factor(rep(c("slow", "intermediate", "rapid"), each = n_per_arm),
                               levels = c("slow", "intermediate", "rapid"))
cohort_inh$NAT2_SLOW <- as.integer(cohort_inh$phenotype == "slow")
cohort_inh$NAT2_RAPID <- as.integer(cohort_inh$phenotype == "rapid")
cohort_inh$dose <- ifelse(cohort_inh$WT < 50, 450, 600)

cohort_lfx <- make_cohort(200, 0.62, 52, 37, 74)
cohort_lfx$CRCL <- rtrunc_lnorm(nrow(cohort_lfx), 81.8, 0.25, 50.5, 136)
cohort_lfx$dose <- ifelse(cohort_lfx$WT < 46, 750, 1000)
cohort_lzd <- cohort_lfx
cohort_lzd$dose <- 600

cohort_summary <- rbind(
  data.frame(cohort = "isoniazid", WT = median(cohort_inh$WT), FFM = median(cohort_inh$FFM),
             mg_per_kg = median(cohort_inh$dose / cohort_inh$WT)),
  data.frame(cohort = "linezolid", WT = median(cohort_lzd$WT), FFM = median(cohort_lzd$FFM),
             mg_per_kg = median(cohort_lzd$dose / cohort_lzd$WT)),
  data.frame(cohort = "levofloxacin", WT = median(cohort_lfx$WT), FFM = median(cohort_lfx$FFM),
             mg_per_kg = median(cohort_lfx$dose / cohort_lfx$WT))
)
knitr::kable(cohort_summary, digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated cohort medians (Table 1: FFM 44.2 / 41.5 / 41.5 kg; 10.0 / 11.5 / 19.1 mg/kg).")
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cohort_inh$FFM) / 44.2 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(median(cohort_lfx$FFM) / 41.5 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

# Simulation

Each virtual participant takes the drug once daily for 14 days. Days 1-7 are
visit 1 (no clofazimine) and days 8-14 visit 2 (clofazimine from day 8), so
both visits reach steady state. As in the study, every dose before the
sampling day is an unobserved occasion and the sampling-day dose is an observed
occasion: OCC = 1 for days 1-6, 2 for day 7, 3 for days 8-13 and 4 for day 14.
The pre-dose sample of each visit therefore belongs to the unobserved occasion
and carries the inflated absorption BOV of linezolid and levofloxacin.

```{r simulate}
obs_grid <- c(seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25), seq(2.5, 12, by = 0.5), seq(13, 24, by = 1))
dose_v1 <- 24 * 6
dose_v2 <- 24 * 13
occ_at <- function(t) ifelse(t < dose_v1, 1L, ifelse(t < 24 * 7, 2L, ifelse(t < dose_v2, 3L, 4L)))

build_events <- function(cohort) {
  per_id <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
    doses <- data.frame(time = seq(0, dose_v2, by = 24), amt = cohort$dose[i], evid = 1L)
    obs <- data.frame(
      time = c(dose_v1 - 1e-3, dose_v1 + obs_grid, dose_v2 - 1e-3, dose_v2 + obs_grid),
      amt = 0, evid = 0L
    )
    ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
    ev$id <- cohort$id[i]
    ev
  })
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(per_id)
  ev$cmt <- "depot"
  ev$OCC <- occ_at(ev$time)
  ev$CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE <- as.integer(ev$time >= 24 * 7)
  covs <- intersect(c("FFM", "CRCL", "NAT2_SLOW", "NAT2_RAPID"), names(cohort))
  ev <- dplyr::left_join(ev, cohort[, c("id", covs)], by = "id")
  ev[order(ev$id, ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}

# A small hmax keeps the solver from stepping over the narrow absorption pulse
# that a short mean transit time with a long transit chain produces.
sim_cohort <- function(mod, cohort, seed) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, build_events(cohort), returnType = "data.frame",
                       hmax = 0.05, maxsteps = 1e6)
  # Visit 1 runs to the end of its 24 h sampling interval at t = 168 h; the
  # visit-1 profile is followed to 24 h only for the NCA.
  in_v1 <- s$time <= dose_v1 + 24
  s$visit <- factor(ifelse(in_v1, "Visit 1: no clofazimine", "Visit 2: with clofazimine"),
                    levels = c("Visit 1: no clofazimine", "Visit 2: with clofazimine"))
  s$tad <- ifelse(in_v1, s$time - dose_v1, s$time - dose_v2)
  s$tad[s$tad < 0] <- 0
  s
}

sim_inh <- sim_cohort(mod_inh, cohort_inh, 20240411)
sim_lzd <- sim_cohort(mod_lzd, cohort_lzd, 20240412)
sim_lfx <- sim_cohort(mod_lfx, cohort_lfx, 20240413)
sim_inh <- dplyr::left_join(sim_inh, cohort_inh[, c("id", "phenotype")], by = "id")

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(sim_inh$Cc), !anyNA(sim_lzd$Cc), !anyNA(sim_lfx$Cc),
  all(sim_inh$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_inh$Cc)),
  all(sim_lzd$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_lzd$Cc)),
  all(sim_lfx$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_lfx$Cc))
)
```

# Replicating the published VPCs

The paper's VPCs show 0-10 h after the observed dose, stratified by visit.
The ribbons below are the simulated 5th-95th percentiles and the lines the
simulated median, with the residual error included (`sim`), as in a VPC.

```{r vpc-helper}
vpc_summary <- function(sim, ...) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(tad <= 10) |>
    dplyr::group_by(..., visit, tad) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
vpc_plot <- function(d, ylab) {
  ggplot(d, aes(tad)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick") +
    labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = ylab) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

```{r fig2-isoniazid, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Kengo 2024: isoniazid by NAT2 phenotype and study visit (simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles)."}
vpc_inh <- vpc_summary(sim_inh, phenotype)
vpc_plot(vpc_inh, "Isoniazid (mg/L)") + facet_grid(visit ~ phenotype)
```

```{r fig3-linezolid-levofloxacin, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kengo 2024: linezolid (top) and levofloxacin (bottom) by study visit (simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles)."}
vpc_both <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(vpc_summary(sim_lzd), drug = "Linezolid"),
  dplyr::mutate(vpc_summary(sim_lfx), drug = "Levofloxacin")
)
vpc_both$drug <- factor(vpc_both$drug, levels = c("Linezolid", "Levofloxacin"))
vpc_plot(vpc_both, "Concentration (mg/L)") + facet_grid(drug ~ visit, scales = "free_y")
```

Read off the published figures, the observed medians peak at about 13-15 mg/L
for linezolid and 10-12 mg/L for levofloxacin, 2-4 h after the dose, and the
isoniazid medians peak at about 5, 3.5 and 2.5 mg/L at 2 h for slow,
intermediate and rapid acetylators. The study drew no sample before 2 h, so the
isoniazid comparison is with the simulated median at 2 h (`median_2h`); the
simulated isoniazid peak itself falls at about 1 h.

```{r vpc-peaks}
peaks <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  vpc_both |> dplyr::group_by(drug, visit) |> dplyr::summarise(peak_median = max(p50), t_peak = tad[which.max(p50)], median_2h = p50[tad == 2], .groups = "drop"),
  vpc_inh |> dplyr::group_by(drug = paste("Isoniazid,", phenotype), visit) |>
    dplyr::summarise(peak_median = max(p50), t_peak = tad[which.max(p50)], median_2h = p50[tad == 2], .groups = "drop")
)
knitr::kable(peaks, digits = 2, caption = "Peak of the simulated median profile.")

pk <- function(drug, visit) {
  v <- peaks$peak_median[peaks$drug == drug & grepl(visit, peaks$visit)]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique peak for ", drug, " / ", visit)
  v
}
# Bounds are the figure read-offs widened for digitisation error; a wrong
# volume, dose or unit moves the peak by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  pk("Linezolid", "Visit 1") > 10, pk("Linezolid", "Visit 1") < 18,
  pk("Levofloxacin", "Visit 1") > 8, pk("Levofloxacin", "Visit 1") < 14,
  pk("Isoniazid, slow", "Visit 1") > 3.5, pk("Isoniazid, slow", "Visit 1") < 7,
  pk("Isoniazid, rapid", "Visit 1") > 1.5, pk("Isoniazid, rapid", "Visit 1") < 4
)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA over the 24 h dosing interval after the observed dose at each visit. The
pre-dose sample is the time-zero record.

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(sim, group_cols) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("id", group_cols, "tad", "Cc")))
  doses <- conc |>
    dplyr::filter(tad == 0) |>
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c("id", group_cols)))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tad = 0, amt = 1)
  f_conc <- stats::as.formula(paste("Cc ~ tad |", paste(c(group_cols, "id"), collapse = " + ")))
  f_dose <- stats::as.formula(paste("amt ~ tad |", paste(c(group_cols, "id"), collapse = " + ")))
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, f_conc),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, f_dose),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result)
}

nca_lfx <- run_nca(sim_lfx, "visit")
nca_lzd <- run_nca(sim_lzd, "visit")
nca_inh <- run_nca(sim_inh, c("phenotype", "visit"))

nca_summary <- function(nca, group_cols) {
  nca |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c(group_cols, "PPTESTCD")))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
    dplyr::rename("Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast)
}
knitr::kable(nca_summary(nca_inh, c("phenotype", "visit")), digits = 2,
             caption = "Isoniazid: simulated median NCA by NAT2 phenotype and visit.")
knitr::kable(nca_summary(nca_lzd, "visit"), digits = 2,
             caption = "Linezolid: simulated median NCA by visit.")
```

## Comparison against the published levofloxacin AUC

The paper reports one exposure summary: the median levofloxacin AUC rose from
140 mg*h/L at visit 1 to 166 mg*h/L at visit 2 (Results paragraph 5,
Figure S3).

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  visit = c("Visit 1: no clofazimine", "Visit 2: with clofazimine"),
  auclast = c(140, 166)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_lfx |> dplyr::select(visit, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference = reference,
  by = "visit",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Levofloxacin AUC0-24: simulated median versus Kengo 2024.")
attr(cmp, "footnote")

auc_med <- nca_lfx |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(visit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
ratio_med <- auc_med$auc[2] / auc_med$auc[1]
stopifnot(
  all(abs(auc_med$auc / reference$auclast - 1) < 0.2),
  # Typical-value ratio is 1 / 0.852 = 1.174; the per-subject between-visit
  # variability (17% CV) spreads the ratio of cohort medians by about 0.02.
  abs(ratio_med - 1 / 0.852) < 0.08
)
```

The simulated median visit-2 / visit-1 AUC ratio is
`r sprintf("%.3f", ratio_med)`, against the published `r sprintf("%.3f", 166 / 140)`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Liver compartment without a volume.** The paper describes isoniazid
  first-pass "through a liver compartment" but reports no liver volume (nor does
  the cited Gausi 2021 model). The model treats the liver as instantly
  equilibrating: the absorbed dose is multiplied by `fh = 1 - eh` and systemic
  drug is cleared at `qh * eh`, with `eh = fu*CLint/(fu*CLint + QH)`. This is the
  form the same group's isoniazid control streams use (see
  `Calderin_2025_isoniazid`), and the single-dose check above confirms it gives
  the well-stirred oral-clearance identity `AUC = dose / (fu * CLint)`. With a
  hepatic flow of 72 L/h a liver of about 1 L would equilibrate within about a
  minute, so the profile difference from an explicit compartment is negligible.
* **Hepatic flow parameterisation.** Table 2 gives QH = 72.4 L/h for a 42 kg-FFM
  participant; it is encoded at that reference and scaled by (FFM/42)^0.75.
  This equals the conventional 90 L/h at 56.1 kg FFM used in the group's other
  models, 90 * (42/56.1)^0.75 = 72.4 L/h.
* **Isoniazid absorption values.** Table 2 footnote e says the absorption
  parameters were fixed to those of Gausi et al. 2021, but the values Kengo 2024
  prints (ka 3.28 1/h, MTT 0.122 h, NN 2.32) are not the isoniazid values in
  Gausi 2021 Table 2 (ka 2.69 1/h, MTT 0.342 h, NN 48.4). The values printed in
  Kengo 2024 are used, as the ones this model was fitted with.
* **Allometric scaling of Q.** Table 2 marks the isoniazid inter-compartmental
  clearance without footnote a, but the text says FFM scaling was applied to
  "all disposition parameters", so Q is scaled with exponent 0.75.
* **Occasion structure.** The paper treats each dose as an occasion and inflates
  the absorption BOV for pre-dose samples after an unobserved dose. The model
  encodes this as four occasions (unobserved and observed dose at each of the two
  visits), with the visit for the between-visit variability derived from the
  occasion. The scaling factor is applied to the BOV of ka, MTT and F (the
  "absorption parameters" of footnote h) and multiplies the random deviate, so
  each inflated variance is the estimated variance times the squared factor.
* **Creatinine-clearance effect.** The paper states a 4.70% increase in
  levofloxacin clearance per 10 mL/min above the median, without printing the
  equation. It is encoded as linear, `1 + 0.0047 * (CRCL - 81.8)`, centred on
  the 81.8 mL/min median of the levofloxacin cohort (Table 1). CRCL is the raw
  Cockcroft-Gault value in mL/min, not BSA-normalised.
* **Clofazimine effect.** Encoded as a time-varying indicator
  (`CONMED_CLOFAZIMINE`), 0 at visit 1 and 1 at visit 2. The study was not a
  cross-over, so the paper cannot exclude that part of the visit-2 change in
  levofloxacin clearance reflects other factors such as clinical improvement.
* **Residual error.** Additive errors are taken as printed. For isoniazid the
  additive error sat at its lower bound, 20% of the LLOQ, and was fixed there.
  The Beal M6 inflation of the additive error for imputed BLQ records applies to
  no simulated observation and is omitted.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weight and creatinine clearance distributions, the
  sex-specific height distributions, and the dose bands (isoniazid 450 mg below
  50 kg and 600 mg otherwise; levofloxacin 750 mg below 46 kg and 1000 mg
  otherwise) are assumptions chosen to reproduce the Table 1 medians; the paper
  does not report its dose bands.
* **Convention-check warnings.** `checkModelConventions()` reports that the
  isoniazid between-visit etas `etabvv_clint_1` / `etabvv_clint_2` have no
  `lclint` parameter to pair with. They act on intrinsic clearance, whose typical
  value is split by NAT2 phenotype into `lclint_slow`, `lclint_int` and
  `lclint_rapid`; the between-subject eta `etalclint` pairs with the same split.
* **Not packaged.** The clofazimine and cycloserine models used in the paper
  are earlier published models (see "Model and source").
